facts.big: What do you want to study?
facts.label: Tour pela faculdade
facts.sub: Na visita, o guia pergunta o que você quer estudar. Diga o que gosta e faça perguntas sobre biblioteca e moradia.

facts.label: Tour guiado
facts.sub: Muitas faculdades têm tours com alunos atuais como guias. Eles mostram a biblioteca, os dormitórios e o refeitório, e respondem perguntas. Leve duas ou três perguntas anotadas e agradeça no fim: “Thank you for the tour.”

facts.label: Moradia no campus
facts.sub: Em muitas faculdades, os calouros moram em dormitórios, às vezes dividindo o quarto com um colega. As regras variam de escola para escola. Pergunte: “Where do first-year students live?” para entender a opção em cada campus.

compare.br: In Brazil, many people choose a course before they enter the university, and the entrance exam decides the place. Campus visits are not always part of the process.
compare.us: In the USA many students visit a campus before applying. They choose a major later, and many first-year students live in a dorm with a roommate.
compare.tip: Prepare two or three questions before a tour: classes, dorms, library hours, scholarships.
compare.ask: What would you study at a US college? Say it in English.

pages.title: A Saturday at a Boston college · 1/3
paragraphs: Clara is seventeen, and she visits a college in **Boston**. It is a sunny Saturday morning. A student guide meets her at the gate. “Hi! **Welcome to our campus**,” the guide says. Her name is Grace.
“Thank you. **I’m thinking about applying**,” Clara says. “Great! **What do you want to study?**” Grace asks. “**I like science and art**,” Clara answers. “We have both. **Follow me**,” Grace says.

pages.title: A Saturday at a Boston college · 2/3
paragraphs: They walk past old red buildings and green grass. Students sit outside with laptops and coffee. Then they stop at a very big building. “**This is the library**,” Clara reads on the sign. “**It’s huge!**” Grace says with a smile. A sign says OPEN 24 HOURS during exams.

“Many students **hit the books** here at night,” Grace says. “They bring **brain food**, like fruit and nuts, and a **study buddy**.” Clara laughs and takes a photo. “**Where do students live?**” she asks. “Many first-year students live in a dorm,” Grace says.

pages.what: Em inglês, cada palavra tem uma sílaba mais forte, e errar o acento muda a palavra. Em português o acento de library cai em outra sílaba, e por isso muita gente não é entendida.
pages.how: Marque a sílaba forte: LI-bra-ri, de-GREE, pro-FES-sor. Diga a sílaba forte mais alta, mais longa e mais clara; as outras ficam curtas. Bata a mesa na sílaba forte.
pages.tip: Procure a sílaba forte no dicionário (o sinal ˈ vem antes dela) e diga a palavra batucando na mesa.

solo: Modele, peça repetição, depois uso livre.
